item.title: From Swastika to Jim Crow: Screening and Discussion — Sun Nov 1, 2:00 PM — Montclair Public Library
item.description:
***From Swastika to Jim Crow*: Screening and Discussion**
Explore an influential, little-known chapter in the history of Black-Jewish relations in America. We'll be screening a documentary film, From Swastika to Jim Crow, based on a book by the same title by Gabrielle Simon Edgcomb. It tells the story of German-Jewish refugees, who, expelled from their homeland by Hitler and the Nazis, found new lives and careers at historically Black colleges and universities in the American South, influencing a whole generation of Black students and professionals.
After the screening, Dr. Lillie Johnson Edwards and Rabbi Julie will discuss the film's significance.
Dr. Edwards is a Drew University Professor Emerita of History and African American Studies.
Co-sponsored by Shomrei & The_Mark: https://themarkmtc.org.
Source: Congregation Shomrei Emunah

item.title: 🥾 Let's Hike!! at Garret Mountain — Fri Nov 6, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! Garret Mountain Yellow and White Loop Trail is a heavily trafficked loop trail located near Woodland Park, New Jersey that features a lake and is good for all skill levels. The trail offers a number of activity options and is best used from March until October.
**PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES EARLY SO WE CAN START ON TIME!**
We will hike a moderate 3 miles. This is **not** a paved trail, please do **not** wear sneakers
We will meet in the **Auto Overlook** parking lot. It’s a one way, you will pass the equestrian, lambert tower and at some point see the sign for AUTO OVERLOOK
As always, we will go at a moderate pace and won’t leave anyone behind. But **please be considerate** of others if you don't think you will be able to hike at a moderate pace for the duration.

Growing up on South Dakota’s Pine Ridge Reservation, Oglala Lakota chef Sean Sherman understood that his people’s food was rich in flavor, heritage, and connection to the land. It was in the midst of a successful restaurant career mainly cooking European cuisines that he realized the lack of understanding about Native American foodways—a revelation that sent him on a journey to learn more about how Indigenous communities have preserved and evolved their cuisines through the centuries. item.description:
Join us in virtual conversation with Brandi Sellerz-Jackson as she talks about her book, On Thriving: Harnessing Joy Through Life’s Great Labors, a moving guide to self-awareness and radical joy that Ms. magazine praised for taking readers beyond survival into presence and pleasure.
Drawing from her experiences as a doula and intimate storytelling from her own life, Sellerz-Jackson guides us through the many phases of these great labors—labors that we can get stuck in, stunting our ability to thrive. Across age, gender, economic status, or background, we all move through the great labor of our relationships, our mental health, grief and loss, and the feeling of being othered. Sellerz-Jackson doesn’t shy away from the pitfalls of these labors but rather challenges us to actively remain present within them and ask ourselves: What do I need to thrive in the space I’m currently in?
